about: The words of the developer's map (site/pages/map.md) that no other kit file holds, read by site/devmap.py. The build holds each part to its source by name and by quote: every method name in api/README.md has a line here and none is extra; every contract page is a row of part (b) and every quoted cell is on that page; every key of the manifest schema is a row of part (c) or a key that describes the app; every screenshot exists. What it does not hold: the hand-written lines (a method's one line, a manifest key's words), which a reviewer checks against chapter 7 and api/README.md; a quote's section; a cell marked none.

methods.scan_barcode: Find the item a barcode, serial number or lot number belongs to, as the till's scan finds it.
methods.get_item_details: Price one line as the shop prices it: the item's rate, discounts and taxes for a customer, price list, store and quantity.
methods.price_check: Both in one call: the scan, then the price of what it found (nothing found: no price).
methods.apply_workflow: Move a record to its workflow's next state, as a user pressing the workflow's button, with that user's rights.
methods.submit: Submit (book) a saved draft record. A till sale at a register with a partner's check in scope is refused here: book it from a till.
methods.bulk_update: Change several records in one call, each with the caller's rights.
methods.get_count: Count the records of a type that match your filters, without reading them.
methods.get_password: Read a password field of a record. Only a user with System Manager may: your app's own user is refused.
methods.get_docinfo: A record's comments, attachments, assignments and change history, as its page in Desk shows them.
methods.add_comment: Write a comment on a record, shown on its page in Desk.
methods.generate_keys: Make a new API key and secret for a user. The retailer's administrator uses it to give a user a key; it replaces the old secret.
methods.get_logged_user: The user your call runs as: check whose key you hold.
methods.get_versions: The versions of the apps installed on the site, to check a feature's build before you use it.
methods.get_role_permissions: Read the rights each role has on a record type.
methods.add_role_permission: Add a role's row of rights on a record type.
methods.update_role_permission: Change one right of a role's row on a record type.
methods.reset_role_permissions: Put a record type's rights back to the product's own.
methods.run_report: Run one of the retailer's reports by name, with its filters (`report_name`, `filters`), and read its columns and rows as Desk shows them. Watch for: a call that names another `user` reads as that user, and a report the retailer switched off is refused.
methods.prepare_report: Queue a background run of a prepared report (such as Stock Balance); it answers the run's record name (a Prepared Report), which you read when it is done. Watch for: it checks no right.
methods.get_gift_card_status: One gift card's status as the till reads it, by its number (`gift_card_no`): its balance, whether it has expired, whether a payment has used it. A Gift Card record names no customer: find a customer's cards in your own records.
methods.material_request_to_stock_entry: A stock movement built from a submitted request for goods, as Desk's Create menu builds it, unsaved: you save it.
methods.sales_order_to_delivery_note: A delivery note built from a submitted order, as Desk's Create menu builds it, unsaved: you save it.
methods.sales_order_to_sales_invoice: A sale built from a submitted order, as Desk's Create menu builds it, unsaved: you save it.
methods.get_batch_qty: A lot's quantity in a store, or a store's lots of an item with stock.
methods.payer_coverage: On a draft Sales Invoice in Desk: the customer's covers, then what one cover pays, sealed into the invoice.
methods.payer_bill_back: Bill a claim the payer rejected back to the customer; it answers the journal booked, once per sale, claim and reason.
methods.check_open: Open a check at a place, or a tab or pre-order named by its label; it answers the check at version 1.
methods.check_add_lines: Add lines to an open check, with no price: the shop prices the check when the table pays at a till.
methods.check_change_line: Change an unsent line nobody is paying, such as its quantity, choices or note (your own lines, or any line with the right to change any).
methods.check_remove_line: Remove a line not yet sent to the kitchen and that nobody is paying.
methods.check_move: Move a check to another place, or to a tab's label.
methods.check_move_lines: Move some lines to another check.
methods.check_split_line: Split part of a line's quantity off.
methods.check_transfer_server: Hand a check to another server, at a shift's handover.
methods.check_edit: Change a check's covers, label, suggested customer or service mode (the mode only until a line has gone to the kitchen).
methods.check_close: Close a check with no open line.
methods.check_mark_sent: Send: the unsent lines (or the named ones) go to their kitchens on the till's kitchen tickets.
methods.check_void_line: Void a whole line the kitchen already has (the kitchen's manager right); a VOID ticket tells the kitchen to stop.
methods.check_comp_line: Take a line off the check free (the Manager preset's right); it is never on the sale.
methods.check_get: Read one check with its lines; locks nothing.
methods.floor_status: The store's sections, places with their status (free, seated, ordered, paying) and tabs.
methods.check_preview: The shop's own price of the open lines at your register, computed when asked, never stored.
methods.check_claim: A till's own, when a check is paid. Refused to your app whatever it is granted.
methods.check_release: A till's own, when a check is paid. Refused to your app whatever it is granted.
methods.check_note_pending: A till's own, when a check is paid. Refused to your app whatever it is granted.
methods.check_clear_pending: A till's own, when a check is paid. Refused to your app whatever it is granted.
methods.check_break_claim: A till's own: end another till's payment of a check. Refused to your app whatever it is granted.
methods.check_print: A till's own: the printed check for the table. Refused to your app whatever it is granted.
methods.station_tickets: A kitchen station's board now (every station's when none is named): tickets sent in the last 12 hours not yet bumped, and 30 minutes of bumped ones to recall.
methods.station_ticket_move: Move one ticket one step, new to started to ready to bumped; the same step again answers already.
methods.item_availability: A store's items that carry a sold-out or hours rule (or the one you name), available now or not and why.
methods.set_item_availability: Mark an item sold out at one store (until a time or until cleared), clear it, or set the hours it is sold; not fenced to your user's stores.

other_calls.what: The event feed: your app's oldest events not yet done, oldest first.
The event feed: mark up to 500 of your events done.
The event feed: mark one event failed, with your note; it comes back on the next read.
A partner page's answer: your server posts the cashier's choice, signed, and the till applies it.
A payment connector's callback: the result of a payment your connector started.

doctypes: Your own record types, each with its fields, permissions and Desk form and list. A settings record is one of them with `issingle`.
custom_fields: A field your app adds to one of the retailer's record types, such as a warranty reference on a sale's line.
property_setters: Changes to how your own fields show
A change to how a field your app added shows on one of the retailer's record types; never a change to the retailer's own fields, and never making a field mandatory, read-only or hidden.
print_formats: A printed layout of a record: a receipt, a label, a price list page.
workflows: Approval states and the buttons that move a record between them, each limited to a role.
notifications: An email or a system message sent when a record changes or on a date.
reports: A report on the retailer's records, built from a query you declare, run in Desk.
workspaces: Your app's page in Desk, opened from the App library: its shortcuts, lists and reports.
number_cards: A figure on a workspace, such as today's sales.
dashboard_charts: A chart on a dashboard or workspace.
dashboards: A page of number cards and charts.
list_settings: The columns and order a Desk list opens with.
links: Your records listed under one of the retailer's, such as pick tasks under a sales order.
sale_attributes: Extra details carried on a sale, such as a delivery number or a boarding pass.
webhooks: A signed call to your service when a record changes.
registered_applications: Your app's event feed, one per app: the record types it follows. The install makes your app's own user with it.
remote_keys: A key on the till that calls your service and shows its answer.
extension_subscriptions: Your service at one of the till's or Desk's extension points: a check before payment, a capture, a partner page, and the rest of part (b).
extension_modules: A certified WebAssembly module at an extension point that takes one (the check before payment and pricing).
desk_actions: A button on a record's form or a list, which sends the record to your service and shows its answer.
save_rules: Rules the retailer's records must meet when saved, applied by iVendNext itself: required fields, limits, sums.
fiscal_readers: Fields a fiscal service may read from a sale and write back, such as a signature.
list_marks: A coloured label on a row of a Desk list.
register_books: The books of a regulated-stock register, such as a controlled-drug register.
allowed_urls: The addresses your service is reached at; the retailer sees them at install, and every call your app's points make goes only there.

points.when: It fires when a user presses it. The server then **re-checks everything the button showed** on the record as SAVED (never the form's copy)
points.sends: Only then does it send exactly the declared fields to your service and judge your answer.
points.answer: **The answer** — HTTP 2xx, a JSON object of at most 64 KB: a `message`
points.limit: 3 seconds to answer unless the subscription allows more, 10 at most. No retry.
points.sees: down, slow or unreachable — *"⟨label⟩ did not answer in time. Check the record before you try again."*

points.when: It fires **when the document is submitted**, from every door: the iVendNext Desk form or list, a data import, and the API.
points.sends: what is sent with every call — the user's login (usually an email address) and language, the company, the record's type and name — the fields that leave the shop
answer: **The answer** — HTTP 2xx, a JSON object of at most 64 KB, one of five:
points.limit: the time to answer (3 seconds unless raised, at most 10)
points.sees: `allow_and_flag` (the default: the submit goes on and the log row is flagged), `refuse` (*did not answer, so this document can't be submitted yet*), or `ask` (*did not answer. Submit anyway?*)

points.what: List the feed under `registered_applications` in your manifest: one feed per app, with every record type it follows in its `events`.
points.when: The engine writes one event per **document step** a change runs, per registered application that follows that record type, after the change commits (a background job, so seconds later).
points.sees: you pull, so a service that is down simply stops pulling. Your events wait, undone, for as long as you are away.

points.what: **Hide** a field nobody uses, **relabel** it in the shop's own word, **require** it on a new customer, or **show** up to three more Item fields and three more Customer fields
points.when: They fire when the till lights up: the rules ride the theme the till reads at boot, and each screen asks them as it draws.
points.sees: The new-customer sheet has no email field, and adding a customer without a phone at the till is refused with *"Phone is required here."*

points.what: A **Retail Fiscal Reader** tells the POS which POS Invoice fields hold that result and what each status value means, so a new country needs no release.
points.when: It fires when a submitted sale changes (the sale's own change hook, after every app's submit), and again whenever the till re-reads a sale that is still waiting
points.sees: **Down:** the sale waits PENDING and the receipt is held.

points.what: A **Retail Label Layout** is data: HTML with placeholders from a closed list.
points.when: It fires when the cashier presses **Print label** on an item's card or on a basket line (phone, counter and tablet alike)
points.sees: The till fills it on the server and opens it in the device's own print dialog, so it prints on any printer the phone, tablet or counter can already reach.

points.what: A coloured label on a row of a shop's Desk list, shown when the row's values say so
points.when: The marks travel with the user's boot info (read at each Desk page load; the declarations themselves are one cached read)
points.sees: to every Desk user who may read the record type — **and only the marks whose every condition field the user may read**.

points.what: Every verb is a call on the partner API: `/api/method/ivendnext_mpos.api.v1.<verb>`, `POST` (the two reads take `GET` too).
points.when: The register's **Table Service** switch (POS Profile, off by default) turns the whole thing on.
points.sees: The till's own floor reads `floor_status` again on each message, polls every 30 seconds while its live link is down, and says *"Not live. Last updated 20:41."* after 90 seconds without one.

points.when: **On scan** — when the cashier scans an item your filter names (its item group, a group below it, or an item field that is set), after the item is found and **before** its line goes on the sale.
points.sends: line: its item_code, item_group, quantity, unit, batch, serial and the code scanned.
points.answer: *allow* (nothing shown), *confirm* (a beep and a yes / no;
points.limit: on scan or a quantity change 1.5 seconds unless raised, 3 at most · on customer add or select 3 seconds unless raised, 10 at most
points.sees: *"⟨label⟩ did not answer. The item can't be added until it does."*

points.when: It fires when the cashier presses Pay, before the payment sheet opens (`stage: "sale"`); before the refund choices open on every refund the till pays (`stage: "return"`)
points.sends: The numbers are the **server's**, never the till's echo. Money is a whole number of minor units with the currency's own digits (`currency_exponent`: 2 for AED, 3 for KWD, 0 for JPY); quantity is in thousandths.
points.answer: allow it, allow it without some tenders, refuse it, ask the cashier a question, or call a manager.
points.limit: 3 seconds unless raised, at most 10 · at most 3 checks per POS Profile, 10 seconds together
points.sees: *"⟨label⟩ did not answer. This sale can't be paid until it does. Try again, or get a manager."*

points.when: iVendNext writes one *Pending* record per sold line inside the sale's own booking, then asks you after the booking commits.
points.sends: the sale's number, the store, the till's POS Profile, the company, the currency, the language, the customer's id, and the line's item code, item group, unit, face value and amount
points.limit: a time to answer (5 seconds unless raised, at most 10)
points.sees: The cashier sees *Waiting for ⟨your label⟩'s code for ⟨item⟩*, with **Try again** and **Print without it**.

points.when: It fires when the cashier presses the page's key on the till, or when a Desk user opens the page
points.sends: Your page learns who is looking at what from a **signed, one-time, five-minute context** in its address
points.answer: on the till your server may **answer once** — a message, Sale Attribute rows, or both — which the cashier confirms like any till key
points.limit: a page that has not loaded in 10 seconds
points.sees: A page that does not load in 10 seconds shows *"⟨label⟩ isn't answering."* with Close; nothing is added to the sale.

points.when: On a sale to a named customer the cashier presses **Payer**; we ask your service which covers the customer holds (`covers`) and the cashier picks one (the only one is taken).
points.sends: We send the customer's record name, the date, the store, the POS Profile and the cashier.
points.answer: you answer each line's two shares: yours and the customer's (`coverage`)
points.limit: the time to answer (at most 5 seconds; 3 when left empty)
points.sees: a service that does not answer in time, errs, fails its signature or answers wrongly means **no cover**: *"⟨label⟩ cannot be reached: the customer can pay it all, or hold the sale."*

points.when: **Every call is a signed POST** to `https://<connector>/paygw/1/<verb>`
points.sends: `{v, site, reference, merchant, amount_minor, currency, currency_exponent, rail, device, payer{phone,email,name,party} (may be empty), payer_code?}`
points.answer: **An Answer** (`authorise`, `status`): `{v, site, reference, outcome, amount_minor?, currency, auth_ref?, correlation_id?, capture_state?, reason?, exists?, instrument?}`
points.limit: every rail's `authorise` has the one 60 s deadline.
points.sees: A preview that times out, is refused or is malformed dims the wallet at the till for that sale; it never raises at the till.

points.what: answered by **your sandboxed module** (a WebAssembly function, see the partner check's section 6 and the Wasm kit). It may only take money **off** a line.
points.when: on the iVendNext POS server, **after every promotion** (item-level and whole-sale), on the promotion-adjusted line, before the line's tax is worked out
points.sees: the basket line names it beside the promotion, *"Member 5% −R 5.00"*, on the phone, the counter and the tablet

points.what: Two readers a print template may call do that, with the rights of the person viewing the print
points.when: Both readers read as the person viewing the print, the way a Desk list does
points.sees: A refused call answers an empty list (or nothing) and the print renders.

points.what: Lines under the store's name (an address, a tax number, a slogan) and lines at the very end (a returns policy, a thank-you in a second language).
points.when: They print on every receipt of that register, on every print route and in the Print sheet's preview, in every frame.
points.sees: The shipped receipts** print the register's header and footer

points.what: A book says which items it takes, which movements enter it, how its lines are numbered and corrected, and which columns it prints, with the source of each.
points.when: Each movement of an item a book takes writes **one Retail Register Line per book it enters, per document row, per batch**, in the same save as the document
points.sees: **the till checks before the tender** and stops a basket that would go below zero, naming who settles it (a count of the book by its count role).

points.when: It fires on a press, and only then: never before payment, never at booking, never on a schedule.
points.sends: When the cashier presses it, the iVendNext POS server sends your service a read-only picture of the sale in progress.
points.answer: You answer with a message for the cashier, Sale Attribute rows for the sale, values for its lines (Transaction Item Attributes), or any of them together.
points.limit: time to answer 3 seconds unless raised, at most 10
points.sees: *"⟨label⟩ did not answer in time. Nothing was added to the sale."*

points.what: A **Retail Save Rule** record names the record type (and the table, for a rule on rows), one of ten kinds, and whether a broken rule **refuses** the save or **flags** it to the *Sales to review* report.
points.when: It fires at **every save** of that record type — a Desk form, an import and an API write alike
points.sees: pattern: *"⟨Field⟩: use letters and digits only."*

points.what: declares that table once, and the till's scan finds the unit: its item, its batch, its serial, and whether it can be sold.
points.when: It fires **only on a miss**: an item barcode, a serial or a batch is found exactly as before and no source is read.
points.sees: A source that cannot be read is logged and skipped, so a misconfigured table can cost a *Not found*, never a sale.

points.what: Each is a call on the partner API, `/api/method/ivendnext_mpos.api.v1.<name>`, under the rights of the user your app signs in as.
points.when: When a till presses *Send*, each kitchen station gets its own ticket
points.sees: There is no cursor to lose: every read is the whole board, so a screen that dropped its connection reads it again and has caught up.

points.when: The cashier taps the wallet's tile with a customer on the sale, sees the balance and the most this sale may use
points.sends: `{v, customer, customer_name, amount_due_minor, currency, currency_exponent, store, sale_ref, lang}`
points.answer: `{eligible, balance_minor, max_redeemable_minor, label, currency, otp_required, reason}` within 3 s
points.sees: A wallet that cannot be used is dimmed with its reason (*"Wallet isn't installed on this site."*, *"Add the customer first."*), never hidden; a wallet that does not answer its preview says so in the opened sheet.

more_points.name: Webhooks
more_points.when: For a booked sale, that is *Sales Invoice* and *POS Invoice* on **Submit**
more_points.sends: a body that names the record and when it changed, and nothing more

more_points.name: The connect, after an install
more_points.when: After the install, the retailer's site connects itself.
more_points.sends: It sends your app its library key, its own address and the secrets the install made.
